newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore construction, housing loan growth firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore construction, housing loan growth firm.

text.p: Overall bank lending continued to slow in January in Singapore but construction and housing loan growth was still surprisingly firm, the latest report on bank credit by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said on Friday.
Bank credit grew 14.6 percent in January year-on-year, the lowest growth rate recorded since October 1994, said MAS, Singapore's de facto central bank.
Analysts said the growth was in line with the recent slowdown in bank loans and not dramatically lower than December's growth rate of 16.5 percent.
"The trend is not new. The latest figure is not a signal of a drastic slowdown in loan growth," said Liew Yin Sze, chief economist with J.M. Sassoon Securities.
He said the last time loan growth was in single digits was in 1993.
MAS said credit extended by banks moderated across the board in January.
Loan growth to the building and construction sectors, which includes housing loans, was 20.8 percent against 22.3 percent in December.
Liew said the figures indicated housing loan growth was still firm despite anti-speculation property curbs the government introduced last May.

"It looks like the housing loan sector is still supporting loan growth. While the number of housing loans may be down, the quantum of each loan is higher because of higher property prices," Liew said.
Heath McIntyre, banking analyst with HSBC James Capel, said housing loan growth may not be that strong as the MAS figure included loans to the construction sector.
"The MAS does not give a breakdown between the two. But I think housing loan growth could be between 15-18 percent," said McIntyre. He said housing loan growth was 17 percent at the end of 1996.
Loans to financial institutions and personal loans fell to 11 percent and 16 percent respectively, down from 15 percent and 20 percent in December, MAS said.
Credit to the transport was down to 17 percent from 20 percent previously while the commerce sector dropped to 19 percent from 11 percent.
Analysts said they expected bank loans grow between 13 and 15 percent in 1997.
